name: debounce-throttle
description: Implement debounce and throttle utility functions for rate limiting

promptLevels.novice: limit how often a function runs
promptLevels.intermediate: implement debounce and throttle functions that limit function execution rate
promptLevels.advanced: create debounce(fn, delay) that delays execution until idle, and throttle(fn, limit) that limits execution rate
promptLevels.expert: Implement `debounce<T extends (...args: any[]) => any>(fn: T, delay: number): T` that delays execution until `delay`ms of inactivity, and `throttle<T extends (...args: any[]) => any>(fn: T, limit: number): T` that ensures at most one execution per `limit`ms. Both should preserve `this` context and arguments. {languageSpecific}

languageInstructions.typescript: Use TypeScript with generics to preserve function types. Export both debounce and throttle functions.
languageInstructions.javascript: Use JavaScript with closure for timer management. Export both debounce and throttle functions.
languageInstructions.javascript-jsdoc: Use JavaScript with JSDoc including @template for function types. Export both functions.

variants.typescript: Implement `debounce<T extends (...args: any[]) => any>(fn: T, delay: number): T` and `throttle<T extends (...args: any[]) => any>(fn: T, limit: number): T` in TypeScript. Preserve this context and arguments. Export both functions.
variants.javascript: Implement `debounce(fn, delay)` and `throttle(fn, limit)` in JavaScript. Use closures. Preserve this context and arguments. Export both functions.
variants.javascript-jsdoc: Implement `debounce(fn, delay)` and `throttle(fn, limit)` in JavaScript with full JSDoc annotations. Export both functions.

testCases.test: let count = 0; const fn = debounce(() => count++, 50); fn(); fn(); fn(); await new Promise(r => setTimeout(r, 100)); console.assert(count === 1, 'Debounce should call once after delay');
let count = 0; const fn = throttle(() => count++, 50); fn(); fn(); fn(); console.assert(count === 1, 'Throttle should call once immediately');
let count = 0; const fn = throttle(() => count++, 50); fn(); await new Promise(r => setTimeout(r, 60)); fn(); console.assert(count === 2, 'Throttle should allow call after limit');
let result = null; const fn = debounce((x) => { result = x; }, 50); fn(1); fn(2); fn(3); await new Promise(r => setTimeout(r, 100)); console.assert(result === 3, 'Debounce should use latest args');
